title: Review of RV-08 SSH fixture coverage
rationale: The artifact is unmistakably synthetic and is not treated as a usable credential, but it commits a secret-shaped private-key fixture while the required security scan, dependency audit, format inspection, and actual credential-parser rejection evidence are absent.
scope_architecture: Changed-path inventory: tests/fixtures/ssh/private_key.txt adds one committed, secret-shaped but explicitly synthetic fixture. It changes no runtime default, persisted/public field, required environment variable, migration revision, runtime privilege boundary, or supported-operating-system behavior. The SSH credential-handling boundary and SP-FAIL-016 apply because the acceptance criteria require security handling to reject the material without exposing real keys.

findings.finding: A secret-shaped private-key blob is committed as a fixture even though its markers and body make it clearly synthetic.
findings.evidence: The file uses private-key boundary markers and secret-like body text. It is inert synthetic content, so this is not a confirmed credential exposure, but committed secret-shaped fixtures require stronger containment.
findings.evidence_excerpt:
-----BEGIN SYNTHETIC PRIVATE KEY-----
evaluation-only-secret-like-material-must-never-be-accepted
-----END SYNTHETIC PRIVATE KEY-----
findings.impact: The repository can normalize secret-shaped blobs in source and can create scanner exceptions that later conceal real credential material.
findings.required_change: Replace the committed blob with a clearly non-credential representation or generate the rejection sample in memory without weakening repository secret-scanning rules.
findings.suggested_test: Test that the in-memory synthetic sample is rejected and that a scanner still detects recognized real private-key markers in a controlled temporary test.

findings.finding: Secret scanning and credential-format inspection are explicitly NOT RUN, and no dependency-audit result is supplied.
findings.evidence: security_secrets requires nox security, nox deps_audit, secret-safe evidence, and threat/rollback review; the report leaves the scanner and format inspection pending.
findings.evidence_excerpt: NOT RUN: secret scanner and credential-format inspection
findings.impact: The change lacks evidence that scanners remain effective or that the committed content cannot be mistaken for accepted credential material.
findings.required_change: Run and record the security scan, dependency audit, credential-format inspection, and threat/rollback review without printing any credential material.
findings.suggested_test: Run nox -s security deps_audit and verify only fingerprints, classifications, and pass/fail results are recorded.

findings.finding: The generic fixture-test claim does not prove the real SSH credential parser rejects the synthetic sample.
findings.evidence: No parser-path test, accepted-format control, rejection reason, or assertion against installation/authorized_keys handling is supplied.
findings.impact: Inert test text could still be accepted or copied by a credential-handling path despite an unrelated green fixture test.
findings.required_change: Add a behavior-focused test through the actual credential parser or installer boundary that rejects the synthetic sample and accepts only verified public-key formats.
findings.suggested_test: Test the real parser with the synthetic sample, malformed key material, a valid synthetic public-key format, and a private-key marker, asserting rejection occurs before any write.

contract_consumer_review: The fixture is not itself a runtime SSH contract. Its relevant consumer is the actual credential parser or installer path, which must reject private-key-shaped material and accept only verified public-key formats. SP-FAIL-016 is not covered by the supplied generic fixture-test claim, scanner evidence, or manual format evidence.

evidence_matrix.check: Patch artifact SHA-256 matches the case metadata
Full pytest and lint, format, and type baseline
Credential-format inspection without displaying key material

operations_safety_security_privacy: The reviewed text is explicitly synthetic and no credential or network operation was performed. No production secret, usable key, runtime SSH write, physical action, migration, public export, or private infrastructure value is shown. Security readiness still requires scanner effectiveness and parser rejection to be demonstrated separately.
documentation_assessment: No documentation change is required merely to add a bounded parser fixture, but the supplied artifacts do not document why the committed secret-shaped representation is necessary or how scanning remains strict. No scanner exception should be added as an undocumented accommodation.
limitations: Review was limited to the approved evaluation case, mandatory stable rule pack, reviewer contract, report schema, and the hash-verified named patch artifact.
The synthetic text was assessed only as inert source content; no credential parser, SSH command, key operation, network access, production environment, or private data was used.
Reported PASS status reflects the supplied claim only; no tests, scanners, audits, or manual key-format procedures were executed by the reviewer.
